exposure: Epidural Analgesia (EA) during Vaginal Birth After Cesarean (VBAC)
outcome: delivery mode (spontaneous or instrumental vaginal delivery)
maternal outcomes (postpartum hemorrhage, oxytocin augmentation, longer second stage of labor)
neonatal outcomes (perinatal mortality, birth weight, Apgar scores, shoulder dystocia rates)
cohort: The study cohort included 17,516 women who underwent a vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC) with or without epidural analgesia, excluding those with chromosomal abnormalities, major malformations, or multifetal gestations.
finding: Epidural Analgesia (EA) during VBAC was associated with higher rates of instrumental delivery, postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), oxytocin augmentation, and a longer second stage of labor, but no significant differences were observed in neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Epidural Analgesia was associated with higher rates of instrumental vaginal delivery.
